mainTopic: The power of צדקה (בנימין הצדיק and מונבז המלך), then the rules for dividing shared property such as a courtyard, field or garden
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of רבא and רב אמי: רב אמי was upset only because nobody told him how the story ended. Two ברייתות then show the power of צדקה. בנימין הצדיק fed a starving woman and her seven sons from his own money, and twenty-two years were added to his life. מונבז המלך gave away his family's treasures in a drought, and he answered his protesting relatives with six contrasts, each backed by a פסוק. The גמרא then returns to the earlier משנה. Buying a house makes a person a resident right away, and the גמרא brings two reports of what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל held. A new משנה follows: shared property is split against one partner's will only if each part keeps its name. If both partners agree, they may split anything except holy writings. The גמרא explains that the four אמות of a courtyard do not count the space in front of the doors. It then brings רב הונא and רב חסדא on dividing a courtyard by doorways, and a ברייתא that supports רב חסדא. It ends with אמימר's rule about a feeding pit, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why רב אמי was upset: he never heard the ending
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב אמי was upset with רבא only because the people telling him the story did not finish it in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They did not finish telling it in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the story from just before this section. רב אמי got upset because he only heard part of the story about רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier question was why רב אמי would be upset that רבא accepted charity money from the non-Jewish queen איפרא הורמיז. The answer is that the full story was never told to him. Had he heard that רבא gave the money to non-Jewish poor people, he would not have objected.

keyTerms.meaning: they finished it (from the root of 'ending' or 'completing')

steps.whatToRemember: רב אמי's anger came from hearing only half the story. It was not a real dispute with רבא.

phrases.english: That they did not finish it in front of him.
phrases.notes: This means רב אמי never heard the end of the story, that רבא gave the money to non-Jewish poor people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous section about why רב אמי was upset.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification: the listener had incomplete information
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אמי truly disapproved of what רבא did.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was only upset because he never heard the full story.

steps.title: בנימין הצדיק feeds a starving family from his own money
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how בנימין הצדיק, who ran the צדקה fund, fed a desperate woman and her seven sons from his own pocket when the fund was empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: They said about בנימין הצדיק that he was in charge of the צדקה fund. Once, during a drought, a woman came and begged him for food. He swore the fund was empty. She said that if he did not help, she and her seven sons would die. So he fed her with his own money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story from a ברייתא to show how great the מצוה of צדקה is. Here בנימין הצדיק goes beyond his job and gives his own money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His official duty was only to give out what was in the public fund, and the fund was empty. Even so, when lives were at stake, he paid out of his own pocket. This sets up the reward that comes in the next step.

phrases.english: It is taught: They said about him,
about Binyamin the righteous,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה מְמוּנֶּה עַל קוּפָּה שֶׁל צְדָקָה;
phrases.english: that he was appointed over the charity fund.
Once, a woman came before him
during years of drought.
She said to him: My master, support me!
He said to her: I swear by the Temple service
that there is nothing in the charity fund!

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לוֹ: רַבִּי, אִם אֵין אַתָּה מְפַרְנְסֵנִי,
phrases.english: She said to him: My master, if you do not support me,
a woman and her seven sons will die!
He got up and supported her from his own money.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל בִּנְיָמִין הַצַּדִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about the greatness of צדקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בנימין הצדיק saved a family by giving his own money when the public fund was empty.

steps.title: The angels plead for בנימין הצדיק and his death decree is torn up
steps.stepSummary: When בנימין הצדיק became deathly ill, the angels argued before הקדוש ברוך הוא that someone who saved eight lives should not die young, and his decree was torn up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some time later he became sick and was close to death. The ministering angels said to הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the world, You said that whoever saves one Jewish life is like someone who saved a whole world. Should בנימין הצדיק, who kept a woman and her seven sons alive, die after so few years? Right away his decree was torn up.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues and shows בנימין הצדיק's reward. The angels use God's own principle to argue that he should live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angels' argument works like a קל וחומר. If saving one life is like saving a whole world, then saving eight lives must earn him life itself. His צדקה literally saved him from death.

keyTerms.meaning: one who keeps a single life alive

phrases.english: After some time he became sick and was close to dying.
The ministering angels said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world, You said:
Anyone who keeps alive one life in Israel
is as if he kept alive an entire world.

phrases.aramaic: וּבִנְיָמִין הַצַּדִּיק, שֶׁהֶחֱיָה אִשָּׁה וְשִׁבְעָה בָּנֶיהָ,
phrases.english: And Binyamin the righteous, who kept alive a woman and her seven sons,
should he die after these few years?
Right away they tore up his decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the reward for the act described in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saving lives through צדקה earned בנימין הצדיק his own life.

steps.title: Twenty-two years were added to his life
steps.stepSummary: A further teaching adds that בנימין הצדיק was given twenty-two extra years of life.
steps.simpleTranslation: A teaching adds: They added twenty-two years to his life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more detail from another teaching. It tells us exactly how much extra life בנימין הצדיק received.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story already said his decree was torn up. This line tells us how long he lived after that: twenty-two more years.
steps.whatToRemember: בנימין הצדיק's personal צדקה saved eight lives and added twenty-two years to his own life.

phrases.english: It was taught: They added to him
twenty-two years on top of his years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to the ending of the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He was granted twenty-two extra years.

steps.title: מונבז המלך gives away his treasures and his family protests
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how מונבז המלך spent his own treasures and his ancestors' treasures on the poor during a drought. His brothers and family ganged up on him in protest.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our Rabbis taught: There was a story with מונבז המלך, who gave away his treasures and his ancestors' treasures during drought years. His brothers and his father's household joined together against him and said: Your ancestors stored up money and added to what their own ancestors had, and you are giving it all away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story about צדקה. This step sets up the family's complaint, which the king answers in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The family's argument is simple: a good king builds up the family wealth, and you are wasting it. This sets up the king's reply, where he turns their idea of 'storing up' on its head.

phrases.english: Our Rabbis taught: There was an incident with King Munbaz,
who gave away his treasures and his ancestors' treasures
during years of drought.
His brothers and his father's household joined together against him,
and they said to him: Your ancestors stored up treasure
and added to what their own ancestors had,
and you are giving it all away!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second, separate story about the value of צדקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מונבז המלך gave away his family fortune to the poor, and his family protested.

steps.title: מונבז answers: I stored above, where no hand can reach
steps.stepSummary: The king gives his first two contrasts: his ancestors stored below and he stored above, and they stored where hands can steal while he stored where no hand can reach.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: My ancestors stored below, and I stored above, as it says: 'Truth will sprout from the earth, and righteousness will look down from heaven.' My ancestors stored in a place where a hand can reach, and I stored in a place no hand can reach, as it says: 'Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne.'
steps.whatsHappening: The king starts answering his family. He argues that he did not waste the money at all; he moved it to a better 'bank.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each contrast has the same pattern: what my ancestors did, what I did, and a פסוק as proof. Money stored on earth can be stolen. צדקה is stored in heaven, right by God's throne, where no one can touch it.

keyTerms.meaning: a hand can reach it (it can be stolen)

phrases.english: He said to them: My ancestors stored below,
and I stored above,
as it says: 'Truth will sprout from the earth,
and righteousness will look down from heaven.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 85:12. 'Righteousness' (צֶדֶק) points to צדקה, which sits up in heaven.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבוֹתַי גָּנְזוּ בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהַיָּד שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ,
phrases.english: My ancestors stored in a place that a hand can reach,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי גָּנַזְתִּי בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין הַיָּד שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ –
phrases.english: and I stored in a place that no hand can reach,
as it says: 'Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The king begins responding to his family's complaint.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדקה is treasure stored in heaven, safe from theft.

steps.title: Treasure that grows, and treasure of souls
steps.stepSummary: The king's next two contrasts: his ancestors' money produced no fruit while צדקה produces fruit, and they stored money while he stored souls.
steps.simpleTranslation: My ancestors stored something that produces no fruit, and I stored something that produces fruit, as it says: 'Say of the righteous that it is good, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.' My ancestors stored treasures of money, and I stored treasures of souls, as it says: 'The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and one who takes souls is wise.'
steps.whatsHappening: The king keeps going with the same pattern, adding two more ways that צדקה is better than a treasury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money sitting in a vault does not grow, but צדקה keeps giving 'fruit,' meaning reward. Also, his ancestors kept coins, while he saved people's lives, which are 'treasures of souls.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲבוֹתַי גָּנְזוּ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין עוֹשֶׂה פֵּירוֹת,
phrases.english: My ancestors stored something that does not produce fruit,
and I stored something that produces fruit,
as it says: 'Say of the righteous that it is good,
for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.'
My ancestors stored treasures of money,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets. The corrected wording adds it.

phrases.english: and I stored treasures of souls,
as it says: 'The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life,
and one who takes souls is wise.'
phrases.notes: משלי 11:30. 'Takes souls' here means winning over and saving people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבוֹתַי גָּנְזוּ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין עוֹשֶׂה פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the king's list of contrasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדקה produces lasting fruit and saves lives, unlike stored money.

steps.title: Stored for myself and for the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: The king's final two contrasts: his ancestors stored for others and for this world, while he stored for himself and for עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: My ancestors stored for others, and I stored for myself, as it says: 'And it will be צדקה for you.' My ancestors stored for this world, and I stored for the World to Come, as it says: 'Your righteousness will go before you, the glory of ה׳ will gather you in.'
steps.whatsHappening: The king finishes his answer with two last contrasts, ending the story of מונבז המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saved money goes to your heirs after you die, so it is really 'for others.' צדקה stays yours, because it is credited to you personally. It also goes with you into עולם הבא, which no bank account can do.
steps.whatToRemember: מונבז המלך's six contrasts: stored above, out of reach, bearing fruit, of souls, for himself, and for עולם הבא. Each one shows that giving צדקה is the truest way to save wealth.

phrases.english: My ancestors stored for others,
and I stored for myself,
as it says: 'And it will be righteousness for you.'
My ancestors stored for this world,
and I stored for the World to Come,
as it says: 'And your righteousness will go before you,
the glory of ה׳ will gather you in.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the king's six-part answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדקה belongs to the giver forever and goes with him to עולם הבא.

steps.title: Buying a home makes you a resident right away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה: someone who buys a house in the city is immediately like the people of the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he bought a house to live in, in the city, he is like the people of the city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and quotes a line from the earlier משנה so it can comment on it. This is a setup line for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a newcomer counts as a resident only after living in the city for a while. This line says that buying a house to live in makes him a resident right away. The next step will ask whose opinion this follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A house to live in, a residence
The people of the city, the full residents

phrases.english: And if he bought a residence in it
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה, and 'it' means the city.

phrases.english: he is like the people of the city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story of מונבז המלך to the wording of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Buying a residence in the city makes a person a resident right away.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who holds in a ברייתא that buying any amount of land at all makes you a resident.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A ברייתא teaches that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: if he bought any amount of land in the city, he is like the people of the city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that our משנה disagrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and it brings a ברייתא to show his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה needs a house to live in. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל goes further: even a tiny piece of land is enough. So the two views are different, and the משנה must follow someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Land of any size, even a tiny amount

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל –
phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
as it is taught in a baraita:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם קָנָה בָּהּ קַרְקַע כׇּל שֶׁהוּא,
phrases.english: If he bought any amount of land in it,
he is like the people of the city.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells us whose opinion the quoted line of the משנה does not follow
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, buying any amount of land makes a person a resident.

steps.title: A second ברייתא quotes him differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this with another ברייתא, where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires land big enough to build a house on.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a different ברייתא teaches that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: if he bought land there that is fit for a house, he is like the people of the city!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that seems to contradict the first one about what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא says any amount of land is enough. The second says the land must be big enough for a house. Both can't be his view, so the גמרא asks how this works.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא (a challenge)
Fit for a house to live in

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
If he bought land there
that is suitable for a residence,
he is like the people of the city!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from the first ברייתא that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds any amount of land is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות quote the same תנא with different amounts of land, so they contradict each other.

steps.title: Two תנאים disagree about his opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that two תנאים disagree about what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל actually said.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two תנאים, and they disagree about the opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. Each ברייתא comes from a different תנא who reported רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not try to make the two ברייתות agree. It accepts that there were two traditions about what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל held. Either way, both versions are less strict than our משנה, which requires an actual house.
steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה requires buying a real house. In רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's name there are two versions: any land at all, or land fit for a house.

phrases.english: It is a dispute between two tanna'im,
and they disagree about the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי תַּנָּאֵי, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two separate traditions about the same תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות report one single view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so they contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Two different תנאים reported his view differently, so there is no real contradiction

steps.title: New משנה: a courtyard needs four אמות for each partner
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a shared courtyard is not split unless each partner would get four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We do not split a courtyard unless there will be four אמות for this one and four אמות for that one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about partners who own property together. One partner cannot force a split of a courtyard if the shares would be too small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a share is only worth something if it is still big enough to use. For a courtyard, the minimum for each partner is four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not split it (one partner can't force a split)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
We do not divide a courtyard
phrases.notes: This is about two partners, where one wants to split and the other doesn't. The court won't force the split.

phrases.english: unless there will be four cubits for this one
and four cubits for that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shared courtyard is split only if each partner gets at least four אמות.

steps.title: A field: nine קבין each, or nine half-קבין according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A field is split only if each share can take nine קבין of seed. רבי יהודה says nine half-קבין is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not a field, unless it has room for nine קבין for this one and nine קבין for that one. רבי יהודה says: unless it has room for nine half-קבין for this one and nine half-קבין for that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the minimum size for splitting a field, and רבי יהודה disagrees about the amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fields are measured by how much seed it takes to plant them. The תנא קמא wants each share to hold nine קבין of seed. רבי יהודה cuts that in half, so a smaller field can still be split.

keyTerms.meaning: קבין, a measure of seed (singular: קַב)

phrases.english: And not a field

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּהּ תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין לָזֶה,
phrases.english: unless there is in it nine kav for this one
phrases.notes: A field's size is measured by how much seed you need to plant it, so this means room to plant nine קבין of seed.

phrases.english: and nine kav for that one.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּהּ תִּשְׁעַת חֲצָיֵי קַבִּין לָזֶה,
phrases.english: unless there is in it nine half-kav for this one
and nine half-kav for that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list with a field
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A field is split only if each share holds nine קבין of seed. רבי יהודה says nine half-קבין.

steps.title: A garden: half a קב each, or a quarter according to רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: A garden is split only if each share can take half a קב of seed. רבי עקיבא says a בית רובע is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not a garden, unless it has room for half a קב for this one and half a קב for that one. רבי עקיבא says: a בית רובע.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the minimum for splitting a garden, and רבי עקיבא gives a smaller amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A garden needs much less than a field, because even a small vegetable patch is useful. רבי עקיבא goes lower still: an area for a quarter-קב of seed for each partner.

keyTerms.meaning: An area that takes a quarter-קב of seed

phrases.english: And not a garden

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּהּ חֲצִי קַב לָזֶה,
phrases.english: unless there is in it a half-kav for this one
and a half-kav for that one.
Rabbi Akiva says:
An area for a quarter-kav.
phrases.notes: That's half of what the first opinion said, enough room to plant a quarter-קב of seed for each partner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list with a garden
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A garden is split only if each share holds half a קב of seed. רבי עקיבא says a quarter-קב.

steps.title: Buildings and other items: enough for each to use
steps.stepSummary: A hall, a small room, a dovecote, a cloak, a bathhouse, an olive press and a watered field are split only if each share is enough to use.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not a hall, a small room, a dovecote, a cloak, a bathhouse, an olive press or a watered field, unless there is enough for this one and enough for that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists more kinds of shared property. It does not give exact sizes. Each share just has to be enough for its normal use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the measure changes from fixed numbers to a practical test: can each partner still use his share the normal way? Half a cloak or half a bathhouse may be useless, so it is not split unless each half still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough for this one to use

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַטְּרַקְלִין, וְלֹא אֶת הַמּוֹרָן,
phrases.english: And not a hall, and not a drawing room,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַשּׁוֹבָךְ, וְלֹא אֶת הַטַּלִּית,
phrases.english: and not a dovecote, and not a cloak,
phrases.notes: Here טלית means a garment, not a prayer shawl.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַמֶּרְחָץ, וְלֹא אֶת בֵּית הַבַּד,
phrases.english: and not a bathhouse, and not an olive press,
and not an irrigated field,
unless there is in them enough for this one
and enough for that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the list to buildings and objects, using a practical standard
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These items are split only if each share is enough for normal use.

steps.title: The general rule: split only if each part keeps its name
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up: if each part keeps the name of the original after the split, we split it. If not, we don't.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: anything that, when it is split, still keeps its name, we split. And if not, we do not split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with one rule that explains all the cases before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half has to still be called a courtyard, a field, a bathhouse, and so on. If a half is so small that it no longer counts as that thing, one partner cannot force the split.
steps.whatToRemember: Shared property is split only if each partner's part still counts as the same kind of thing (a courtyard, a field, a bathhouse). The sizes in the משנה are examples of this one rule.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
Anything that, when it is divided, retains its name
we divide;
and if not, we do not divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pulls all the listed cases together into one rule
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Split shared property only if each part keeps the name of the original item.

steps.title: The size rules apply only when one partner refuses
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits all the minimum-size rules to a case where the partners do not both want to divide. If both agree, they may divide even smaller shares.
steps.simpleTranslation: When do these rules apply? When the two partners do not both want to split. But if both want to split, they may divide even if the shares are smaller than these sizes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains when all the size rules from the earlier steps apply. They apply only when one partner is forcing a split on the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The minimum sizes protect a partner who does not want to split. That partner cannot be forced into a share too small to use. If both partners agree, nobody needs that protection, so they may split even a tiny piece.

phrases.english: When? When the two of them do not both want to split;
but when both of them want to,
even with less than this, they may divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits all the size rules in steps 13-17 to a case where one partner refuses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The minimum sizes apply only when one partner refuses. If both agree, they may split even smaller shares.

steps.title: Holy books are never cut up
steps.stepSummary: Even when both partners agree, כתבי הקודש may not be divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: But holy writings may not be divided, even if both partners want to.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one exception to the rule it just gave. Holy books may not be split even when both partners agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Agreement between the partners normally allows any split. Holy writings are the exception, because cutting them apart is not respectful.

keyTerms.meaning: holy writings, scrolls of the books of תנ״ך

steps.confusionAlert: Holy writings are still property that two people can own together. The only point is that this item may not be cut apart, even with agreement.

phrases.english: But holy writings,
even if both of them want to,
they may not divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם רוֹצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an exception to the rule of step 18 that partners who both agree may split.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כתבי הקודש are never divided, even when both partners agree.
steps.whatToRemember: The size rules protect a partner who refuses to split. If both agree, anything may be split except holy writings.

steps.title: The four אמות are on top of the doorway space
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי in the name of רבי יוחנן says the four אמות each partner needs in a חצר do not count the space in front of the doorways.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the four אמות the משנה spoke of are not counting the space in front of the doors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It explains the four אמות rule for a חצר from step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each house already gets some space in front of its door, and that space is not split. רבי יוחנן says the four אמות must be in addition to that space. So each partner really needs more than four אמות of courtyard in total.

keyTerms.meaning: the discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The four cubits that they mentioned
are besides those of the doorways.
phrases.notes: Each house gets a strip in front of its door for loading and unloading. That strip doesn't count toward the four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's explanation of the חצר rule from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four אמות per partner are in addition to the doorway space.

steps.title: A ברייתא says eight אמות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a חצר is divided only if each partner gets eight אמות. This is brought as support for רבי אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches this too: we do not divide a courtyard unless there are eight cubits for one partner and eight for the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי אסי. The next steps explain how this ברייתא proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives eight אמות, not four. Eight fits if you add four אמות of doorway space to the four אמות of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא also teaches this (a support)

phrases.english: It was also taught in a baraita like this:
We do not divide the courtyard

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּהּ שְׁמוֹנֶה אַמּוֹת לָזֶה,
phrases.english: unless it has eight cubits for this one,
and eight cubits for that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to back up רבי אסי's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אסי's rule that the four אמות do not include the doorway space.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that requires eight אמות per partner.

steps.title: But the משנה says four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that our משנה says four אמות, not eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in our משנה: four cubits for this one and four cubits for that one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא seems to clash with the משנה. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא says eight and the משנה says four, they seem to disagree. Showing this clash is the first half of the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't we learn in our משנה

phrases.english: But we learned in the Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת לָזֶה, וְאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת לָזֶה!
phrases.english: Four cubits for this one, and four cubits for that one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the ברייתא's eight against the משנה's four.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's number of eight אמות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires only four אמות, so how can the ברייתא require eight?

steps.title: So the ברייתא follows רבי אסי
steps.stepSummary: The only way the משנה and the ברייתא fit together is רבי אסי's rule. So the ברייתא supports him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that it follows רבי אסי. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The ברייתא's eight is four plus the doorway space, just as רבי אסי said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה counts only the four usable אמות. The ברייתא counts those four plus the four in front of the door. Both are correct, and רבי אסי is proven.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it, it is proven
in line with the view of רבי...

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it: it is like Rabbi Asi;
learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the clash from step 22 by using רבי אסי's rule, which proves him right.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא's eight אמות are the משנה's four plus the doorway space, as רבי אסי said.
steps.whatToRemember: Four usable אמות plus four by the door makes eight. The משנה and the ברייתא agree.

steps.title: Another version: the משנה and ברייתא contradict
steps.stepSummary: Some tell the passage differently. They start by pointing out that the משנה says four אמות and the ברייתא says eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some present it as a contradiction. We learned: we do not divide a courtyard unless there are four cubits for each partner. But a ברייתא teaches eight cubits for each!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way the discussion was told. Here it opens with a contradiction, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The facts are the same as in the first version, but the order changes. Here the two sources are set against each other first, and רבי אסי's rule comes only afterward as the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: some present them as a contradiction

phrases.english: And there are those who set them against each other:
We learned: we do not divide the courtyard

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּהּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת לָזֶה,
phrases.english: unless it has four cubits for this one,
and four cubits for that one.
But it was taught: eight cubits for this one,
and eight cubits for that one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells steps 20-23 in a different order, starting with the contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the משנה (four אמות) fits with the ברייתא (eight אמות)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sources give two different minimum sizes for the same case.

steps.title: רבי אסי's rule answers the contradiction
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רבי אסי's statement answers the contradiction. The four אמות do not include the doorway space.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the four cubits they mentioned are besides the space of the doorways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 24 with רבי אסי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי אסי's words are an answer, not a statement standing on its own. The משנה counts four usable אמות, and the ברייתא adds the four by the door, so the total is eight.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The four cubits that they mentioned
are besides those of the doorways.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source counts a different area
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא disagree about the minimum size of a share.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה counts only the usable four אמות. The ברייתא also counts the four אמות in front of the door.

steps.title: רב הונא: split the חצר by number of doors
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says a חצר is split according to how many doorways each partner has opening onto it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: a courtyard is divided according to its doorways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question: how do we divide a חצר when one house has more doors than the other? רב הונא gives the first view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב הונא's view, a partner with more doors onto the חצר gets a bigger share. The whole חצר is divided by counting doors.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
A courtyard is divided according to its doorways.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: חָצֵר מִתְחַלֶּקֶת לְפִי פְּתָחֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the minimum size to how the חצר is actually shared out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole חצר is divided in proportion to each partner's number of doorways.

steps.title: רב חסדא: four אמות per door, then split the rest equally
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says each doorway gets four אמות, and the rest of the חצר is split equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: we give four cubits for each doorway, and the rest they divide equally.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא disagrees with רב הונא about how to divide a חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב חסדא, having more doors only gets you more doorway space. Each door gets four אמות. Everything left over is split fifty-fifty, no matter how many doors each partner has.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא divides the whole חצר by number of doors. רב חסדא gives four אמות per door and splits the rest equally.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתְנִין אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת לְכׇל פֶּתַח וּפְתַח,
phrases.english: We give four cubits for each and every doorway,
and the rest they divide equally.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: נוֹתְנִין אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת לְכׇל פֶּתַח וּפְתַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opinion that disagrees with רב הונא in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each doorway gets four אמות, and the rest of the חצר is split equally between the partners.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says each doorway gets four אמות, and the rest of the חצר is divided equally, just as רב חסדא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא like רב חסדא: Doorways in a חצר get four אמות each. If one partner has one doorway and the other has two, the one with one doorway takes four אמות. The one with two doorways takes eight אמות. They split the rest equally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says exactly what רב חסדא said in the last step. This backs up his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said the whole חצר is split by number of doorways. רב חסדא said only four אמות per doorway follow the doorways, and the rest is split equally. The ברייתא gives extra space per doorway but splits the rest equally, so it matches רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא in line with him (support for an אמורא)

steps.whyThisMatters: A ברייתא matching רב חסדא's exact rule gives his view strong support against רב הונא's view in step 26.

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with רב חסדא:

phrases.aramaic: פְּתָחִים שֶׁבֶּחָצֵר – יֵשׁ לָהֶן אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: Doorways that open to a courtyard have four amos each.
If this one had one doorway,
and that one had two doorways;

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ פֶּתַח אֶחָד – נוֹטֵל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: the one who has one doorway takes four amos,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי פְתָחִים – נוֹטֵל שְׁמוֹנֶה אַמּוֹת;
phrases.english: and the one who has two doorways takes eight amos;
and they divide the rest equally.
phrases.notes: This is the key line. The rest is split half and half, not by doorways, and that is why it fits רב חסדא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting רב חסדא's rule from step 27.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule: four אמות per doorway, the rest split equally
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that gives four אמות per doorway and splits the rest equally

steps.title: The ברייתא adds the case of a very wide doorway
steps.stepSummary: If a doorway is eight אמות wide, the owner gets eight אמות in front of it and four אמות into the חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one partner had a doorway eight אמות wide, he takes eight אמות opposite the doorway, and four אמות in the חצר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going with a new case: one extra-wide doorway. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal doorway gets a four-by-four space. A wide doorway gets space along its whole width of eight אמות. The words "four אמות in the חצר" are unclear, so the גמרא asks about them next.

keyTerms.meaning: Opposite or in front of the doorway

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה לָזֶה פֶּתַח רָחָב שְׁמוֹנֶה אַמּוֹת –
phrases.english: If this one had a doorway eight amos wide,
he takes eight amos opposite the doorway,
and four amos in the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה לָזֶה פֶּתַח רָחָב שְׁמוֹנֶה אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An eight-אמה-wide doorway gets eight אמות opposite it and four אמות into the חצר.

steps.title: What do the four אמות in the חצר mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by "four אמות in the חצר."
steps.simpleTranslation: "Four אמות in the חצר": what are they doing here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by the ברייתא's words and asks what they mean. אביי will answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "four אמות in the חצר" sounds like a separate extra piece of land, which makes no sense next to the eight אמות. The גמרא wants to know how these two numbers fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their purpose? What are they doing here?

phrases.english: Four amos in the courtyard,
what are they doing here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the last phrase of the ברייתא in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the four אמות in the חצר relate to the eight אמות opposite the doorway

steps.title: אביי: eight אמות long and four אמות deep
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the owner gets a strip eight אמות along the length of the חצר and four אמות into its width.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, this is what the ברייתא means: he takes eight אמות along the length of the חצר and four אמות along the width of the חצר.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. The two numbers describe one rectangle, not two separate pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eight אמות run along the wall, matching the doorway's width. The four אמות go out from the wall into the חצר. So the owner gets a strip eight by four, the normal four-אמה depth stretched across the whole doorway.
steps.whatToRemember: A wide doorway gets a strip as wide as the doorway and four אמות deep. The rest of the חצר is still split equally, like רב חסדא said.

phrases.english: אביי said: This is what it is saying:
he takes eight amos along the length of the courtyard,
and four amos along the width of the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The eight and four אמות are the length and width of one strip in front of the doorway.

steps.title: אמימר: A feeding pit gets four אמות on every side
steps.stepSummary: אמימר teaches that a pit for animal food gets four אמות of space on each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: A pit for animal food has four אמות on each and every side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new related rule from אמימר. A feeding pit in a shared חצר gets four אמות around it in every direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like a doorway gets space in front of it, a feeding pit gets space so animals can stand around it and eat. Since it can be used from every side, the space goes all around it.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit or trough for holding animal food

phrases.english: אמימר said:
This pit for animal food

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת לְכׇל רוּחַ וָרוּחַ.
phrases.english: has four amos on each and every side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from doorways to another item in a חצר that gets its own space.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A feeding pit gets four אמות on every side.

steps.title: The rule applies only when the pit has no set entrance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits אמימר's rule: it applies only when the pit has no special entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we only said this when the pit does not have its own set entrance,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows אמימר's rule. The four אמות on every side apply only when the pit is reached from all sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If animals can come at the pit from any side, it needs space all around. If it has one set entrance, there is no reason to give space on every side. The sentence continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: And we only said this when
It has its own set entrance

phrases.english: And we said this only
where it does not have its own set entrance,
phrases.notes: So the animals reach it from every side. That is why it needs space all around.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא מְיַיחַד לֵיהּ פִּתְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of אמימר's rule from step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four אמות on every side apply only to a pit without its own set entrance.
